energy-momentum-relation.title: Energy-Momentum Relation
energy-momentum-relation.reference_prose: The relativistic energy-momentum relation is a fundamental equation relating the rest mass, total energy, and momentum of a massive particle or system of particles. It is given by E^2 = (pc)^2 + (mc^2)^2, which relates energy, momentum, speed of light, and invariant rest mass, ensuring compatibility with special relativity.

variable-mass.title: Variable Mass Systems
variable-mass.reference_prose: A variable mass system is a collection of matter whose mass changes with respect to time, typically due to accretion or ejection of mass, such as a rocket or jet engine. The motion of such a system requires a generalized formulation of Newton's second law to account for momentum transfer and reactive thrust from the lost or gained mass.

weak-form-newton.title: Weak Form of Newton's Third Law
weak-form-newton.reference_prose: The weak form of Newton's third law of motion states that for any two interacting particles, the force exerted by the first particle on the second is equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the force exerted by the second particle on the first. This condition is sufficient to ensure the conservation of total linear momentum in an isolated system of particles.

strong-form-newton.title: Strong Form of Newton's Third Law
strong-form-newton.reference_prose: The strong form of Newton's third law of motion states that, in addition to being equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, the forces of action and reaction between any two particles must also be directed along the line joining their centers. This additional collinearity constraint is required to guarantee the conservation of total angular momentum in a system of particles.

universal-gravitation.title: Universal Gravitation
universal-gravitation.reference_prose: Newton's law of universal gravitation states that every particle attracts every other particle in the universe with a force proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centers. This force acts along the line intersecting their centers.
